definition: In mathematical optimization, linear-fractional programming (LFP) is a generalization of linear programming (LP).
details: Whereas the objective function in a linear program is a linear function, the objective function in a linear-fractional program is a ratio of two linear functions. A linear program can be regarded as a special case of a linear-fractional program in which the denominator is the constant function 1. Formally, a linear-fractional program is defined as the problem of maximizing (or minimizing) a ratio of affine functions over a polyhedron, where x ∈ R n {\displaystyle \mathbf {x} \in \mathbb {R} ^{n}} represents the vector of variables to be determined, c , d ∈ R n {\displaystyle \mathbf {c} ,\mathbf {d} \in \mathbb {R} ^{n}} and b ∈ R m {\displaystyle \mathbf {b} \in \mathbb {R} ^{m}} are vectors of (known) coefficients, A ∈ R m × n {\displaystyle A\in \mathbb {R} ^{m\times n}} is a (known) matrix of coefficients and α , β ∈ R {\displaystyle \alpha ,\beta \in \mathbb {R} } are constants. The constraints have to restrict the feasible region to 0\}}"> { x | d T x + β > 0 } {\displaystyle \{\mathbf {x} |\mathbf {d} ^{T}\mathbf {x} +\beta >0\}} , i.e. the region on which the denominator is positive. Alternatively, the denominator of the objective function has to be strictly negative in the entire feasible region.

explainer.lead: Linear-fractional programming generalizes linear programming by optimizing a ratio of two linear functions instead of a single linear function. It matters because it covers ratio-based objectives while remaining a polyhedron-constrained optimization problem.

tiers.eli5: Instead of maximizing one total, you maximize one total divided by another, like getting the best return per unit of cost.
tiers.practitioner: Used when the objective is a ratio of linear functions over a polyhedron; a pitfall is forgetting that ordinary linear programming is only the special case where the denominator is the constant 1.
tiers.paperLevel: Maximize or minimize a ratio of affine functions over a polyhedron, with x in R^n; linear programming is the special case with denominator equal to the constant function 1.

explainer.example: Maximizing a ratio of two linear functions subject to polyhedron constraints; setting the denominator to the constant 1 reduces it to a standard linear program.
